Spatial framework bridges

Source: vignettes/spatial-framework-bridges.Rmd
spatial-framework-bridges.Rmd

dedicated bridge functions. Each bridge processes exactly one image at a time and never wraps the target framework’s analysis or plotting API.

Choose the interface

Goal Interface Returned object Plotting
Move one Seurat image into Giotto srt_to_giotto() Native Giotto object Giotto’s native plotting API

Giotto version boundary

Current Giotto Suite releases split analysis functions and object/conversion helpers across the Giotto and GiottoClass namespaces. scop resolves these optional functions at runtime and does not add Giotto to Imports, Depends, or Suggests.

The forward bridge selects seuratToGiottoV5() for Seurat 5 and seuratToGiottoV4() for Seurat 4. The reverse bridge selects giottoToSeuratV5() for Seurat 5 and giottoToSeuratV4() for Seurat 4. These converters are expected from a current GiottoClass installation. If an older Giotto installation does not provide them, update Giotto before using the bridges.

GitHub documentation build contract

in this article are deliberately shown but not evaluated during the GitHub pkgdown build, so publishing the documentation does not select or install a particular framework generation. Reference pages are still parsed and indexed, and dependency checks run when a user calls a bridge.

On pull requests, the GitHub workflow validates the complete reference index. After a merge to main, changes that include source, reference, or pkgdown configuration files trigger a full site build; an article-only change can use the narrower article build. The scheduled full build remains the compatibility check against the then-current dependency ecosystem.

Ordinary package and pkgdown checks remain independent of a user’s Giotto installation. A Giotto compatibility failure must be classified as a scop regression, an upstream Giotto API regression, or a runner failure.

Single-image conversion

The bridges process exactly one image at a time:

  • a single image is selected automatically;
  • a multi-image object requires an explicit image;
  • an unknown image name is rejected;
  • slices are never merged implicitly.
gobject <- srt_to_giotto(spatial, image = "slice1")
spatial_roundtrip <- giotto_to_srt(gobject)
